A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EpiCoder research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original EpiCoder fine-tuning and benchmark evaluations, XFileDep results, and quantitative analyses of synthesized code complexity, diversity, leakage and data scaling.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds training-data-size comparisons, manual XFileDep validation and revised file-level evaluation results.

M1.justification: Feature extraction, tree evolution, frequency estimation, temperature-based sampling and execution-guided refinement remain unchanged. V1 Algorithms 1 and 2 correspond to v2 Algorithms 2 and 1. The retained appendix prompts establish that compatible-feature selection and task/code generation already existed despite revised main-text descriptions.

E1.justification: The training sources, five function-level benchmarks, Python cross-file completion task and LLaMA-Factory repository case are retained. Smaller training subsets and XFileDep quality filtering change sample selection without establishing new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds comparisons with Magicoder-DS, distinct from Magicoder-S-DS, and SelfCodeAlign-CQ-7B in Tables 5–6. EvoEval adds Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct and Codestral-22B-v0.1. The consolidated Table 1 also substantially changes comparator membership, including removing GPT-3.5-Turbo from HumanEval/MBPP and replacing GPT-4o with GPT-4-Turbo in BigCodeBench.

E3.justification: V2 Appendix B.2 adds manual question–solution consistency checks, reducing XFileDep from 930 to 466 problems and changing the evaluation sample. Section 4.3 introduces 75k-example DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B and 74k-example CodeQwen-7B training comparisons. These are substantive evaluation changes; the existing greedy decoding and XFileDep execution settings remain.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds a focused analysis testing whether EpiCoder's advantages persist with comparable training-data quantities against Magicoder, WaveCoder and SelfCodeAlign. Existing scaling, leakage, complexity, diversity and repository case analyses are retained, often relocated to appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run counts, random-seed reporting, confidence intervals or significance tests. The same complexity means, medians and standard deviations appear in v1 Table 6 and v2 Table 12; these describe variation across code samples.

E6.justification: V2 Tables 5–6 add results for the 75k and 74k models, with reported averages of 51.2 and 62.6. Figure 4 replaces XFileDep scores of 65.7/68.8 for EpiCoder-DS/Qwen with 68.2/69.7 on the reduced test set, so these are not same-setting gains. Complexity-score percentage comparisons are corrected from 1.08%/1.74% to 32.6%/52.5% without changing table scores. V2 retains old XFileDep values in Figure 1 and inconsistently reports WaveCoder EvoEval as 43.6 in Table 5 versus 42.0 in Table 7.

T1.justification: Equation 1, sibling-frequency estimation, sampling mathematics and the Halstead-derived metric definitions are retained. Algorithm relocation and explicit output labels do not introduce new mathematical reasoning, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain controllable feature-tree synthesis, 433k instruction examples, strong function/file-level EpiCoder performance and potential repository-level synthesis. The introduction's explicit 7.4-point BigCodeBench-Hard comparison foregrounds results already present in v1 without changing the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: V2 Section 4.3 explicitly interprets comparable-data-size results as evidence for data quality and evolutionary enhancement beyond training quantity, including improved generalization. The existing complexity, diversity, leakage and repository-scalability interpretations largely remain, with no substantive new limitations discussion.

D1.justification: V2 supplies an explicit code-and-data repository link in the abstract, whereas v1 only refers to released code. Appendix B.2 adds manual-review criteria and reviewer qualifications. Most implementation information and prompts persist, although some displayed feature-extraction prompt details are further abridged.

R1.justification: V2 adds SelfCodeAlign and OctoPack citations and expands coverage of code search, retrieval-augmented generation and tree-based code-generation research. The LIMA citation is removed. The central positioning around feature-based synthetic instruction data remains; publication updates and consolidated duplicate references are not new works.

P1.justification: The abstract and main narrative are extensively condensed and reorganized. Benchmark descriptions, feature-evolution pseudocode, the file-generation illustration, and scaling/leakage analyses move into reorganized appendices. Section headings and explanations are revised, the appendix contents page is removed, and an Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column preprint layout to two-column conference layout. Benchmark results are consolidated into Table 1, Tables 5–6 are added, Figure 1 becomes a radial chart, and a new FullStackBench bar chart redisplays existing results. The XFileDep flowchart adds human checking, while numerous retained displays are relocated and resized.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens two central aspects of empirical validity: expert question–solution review supplements v1's automated XFileDep filtering, and matched-size Magicoder/SelfCodeAlign comparisons address the previously uncontrolled role of training-data quantity. These changes improve confidence in the benchmark and the synthesis approach's benefits; explicit code/data access also helps reproducibility. Stale XFileDep overview scores and inconsistent WaveCoder results are material reporting flaws, but do not outweigh those gains.
